For problems with the Python setup, extra downloads or your own Python
environment, see [Installation and setup](installation.html). For GPUs, see
the [GPU](gpu.html) article.


## Reporting a problem

`birdnet_sitrep()` shows which Python environment birdnetR uses:

```{r}
birdnet_sitrep()
#> python_version: 3.12.14
#> python_executable: /home/user/.cache/uv/archive-v0/0MLD8yprGexELXHg/bin/python
#> birdnet_version: 1.4.0
#> runtimes: onnxruntime, ai_edge_litert
```

- `python_version`, `python_executable`: the Python that birdnetR runs on.
- `birdnet_version`: the version of the `birdnet` Python package.
- `runtimes`: the installed inference runtimes (any of `onnxruntime`,
  `ai_edge_litert` (LiteRT), `tensorflow` and `torch`).

Please include this output when you
[report a bug](https://github.com/birdnet-team/birdnetR/issues).

After birdnetR has installed TensorFlow or PyTorch during a session (see
[Extra downloads](installation.html#extra-downloads)), `python_executable`
points to a different folder than before. That is expected: reticulate adds the new packages as an
extra layer on top of the existing environment.


## Long wait on the first load

The first load of a model can take several minutes without visible progress:
birdnetR is downloading Python packages, and for TensorFlow or PyTorch that is
600 MB to several GB. See
[Download progress](installation.html#download-progress).


## Long pause after prediction

If you notice a long pause after BirdNET has finished processing your audio but before you get the results, this is probably the conversion from Python to R in `as.data.frame()`. This is particularly noticeable when:

- processing long audio files (> 20 minutes),
- using low confidence thresholds that generate many predictions (`min_confidence < 0.1`),
- working with little memory.

### Solution: use `birdnet_write()`

For large results, use `birdnet_write()` to write them directly from Python to a file (CSV, Parquet, or NumPy) without converting them to an R data frame first.

```{r}
model <- birdnet_load()
predictions <- birdnet_predict(model, audio_path)

# Write directly from Python - no R conversion needed
birdnet_write(predictions, "results.csv")
```

For tips on processing many files, see
[Process many files](birdnetR.html#process-many-files).


## High memory or CPU use

`birdnet_predict()` and `birdnet_encode()` start several worker processes, and
each loads its own copy of the model. On the CPU, birdnet starts one worker per
physical core (fewer when memory is short) and keeps all cores busy. Full CPU
load during a run is expected.

If memory runs out, or the computer becomes unresponsive, lower `n_workers` and
`batch_size`:

```{r}
predictions <- birdnet_predict(model, files, n_workers = 2L, batch_size = 1L)
```

- `n_workers` is the number of model copies in memory. TensorFlow and PyTorch
  workers need more memory than ONNX Runtime ones.
- `batch_size` is the number of segments each worker processes at once. Larger
  values need more memory.

Fewer workers mainly save memory: birdnet gives each worker more CPU threads,
so the CPU stays busy. If a worker is killed because memory ran out, birdnet
stops with an error that names the worker.

With `device = "GPU"`, birdnetR starts one worker per GPU. A larger
`n_workers` puts another copy of the model on the GPU for each extra worker;
see [Workers and batch size](gpu.html#workers-and-batch-size).


## Parallel processing

Don't run birdnetR inside `parallel` or `future` workers (for example with
`parallel::parLapply()`, `future.apply::future_lapply()` or `furrr`). Each
worker is a fresh R session without birdnetR's Python setup, so birdnet does
not work reliably there (see
[#56](https://github.com/birdnet-team/birdnetR/issues/56)).

`birdnet_predict()` and `birdnet_encode()` already run in parallel. Pass all
files in one call and set the number of parallel workers with `n_workers`:

```{r}
predictions <- birdnet_predict(model, files, n_workers = 8L)
```


## Harmless console messages

- Decoding MP3 files (for example the bundled `soundscape.mp3`) can print
  libmpg123 errors such as `part2_3_length ... too large`. The results are not
  affected.
- TensorFlow prints CUDA or XLA log lines on computers without an NVIDIA GPU,
  for example `failed call to cuInit`. You can ignore them.
- uv prints `warning: The --torch-backend option is experimental` when it
  installs PyTorch for a GPU.
- With PyTorch, each worker prints a `FutureWarning` that `torch.jit.load` is
  deprecated.
- The ROCm build of PyTorch (AMD GPUs) prints
  `(null): No such file or directory`, in your system's language, when it
  starts.
